name: LJC18A3-H-Z/BX capacitive proximity switch
description: Capacitive proximity switch in an M18 threaded barrel: senses metal and non-metal objects (plastic, glass, wood, water, grain, liquid through a plastic tank wall) within about 1-10 mm of its face, range set by the trimpot on the back. Gives on/off only. NPN open-collector output, normally open: OUT is pulled LOW while an object is detected and needs a pull-up (to 3.3 V, never to the sensor supply) otherwise; sinks up to 300 mA. Needs a separate 6-36 V DC supply (12-24 V nominal). Sold as: LJC18A3-H-Z/BX capacitive proximity sensor switch, NPN NO, DC 6-36 V (M18 barrel about 75 mm long, 3-wire lead: brown V+, black OUT, blue GND).
eli5: A tube that notices when almost anything (metal, plastic, water, your hand) comes within a centimetre of its tip, without touching it, and tells your board. It needs its own 12 V power supply.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Brown wire: supply, 6-36 V DC from a separate supply (12 V or 24 V typical). Not the board's 3V3/5V.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Black wire: NPN open-collector output, pulled LOW while an object is detected, otherwise open. Needs a pull-up to 3.3 V (Sparkbench adds 10 kOhm to 3V3); never pull it up to the 6-36 V supply. Sinks up to 300 mA.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Blue wire: 0 V. Join it to the supply negative and the microcontroller GND.

supplierQuery: LJC18A3-H-Z/BX capacitive proximity sensor NPN NO 6-36V
buildNotes: Wires: brown = VCC (6-36 V DC), black = OUT, blue = GND (standard 3-wire DC sensor colours). Check the label on the cable: the /BY version is PNP and must not be wired this way.
Power the brown wire from a separate 6-36 V DC supply (12 V is typical), never from the board's 3V3/5V. Join the supply negative, the blue wire and the microcontroller GND.

OUT is an NPN open collector, active LOW: it reads 0 while an object is in range. Pull it up to 3V3 with 4.7-10 kOhm (the driver also enables the internal pull-up). Never pull it up to the 12/24 V supply.

Extra protection recommended: in some units the indicator LED is fed from the supply through the output, so an unloaded OUT can float to several volts. A Schottky diode in series (cathode to the black wire, anode to the GPIO and its 3V3 pull-up) or a PC817 optocoupler keeps the sensor's supply off the GPIO.

Set the range with the small trimpot on the back (the LED lights while it detects). Adjust it with the target in place: for a liquid level through a tank wall, turn it until the LED just lights with liquid and goes out without.
Capacitive sensors react to anything nearby, including the mounting bracket, hands and moisture. Mount the face clear of other objects and keep it dry.

example.code:
from ljc18a3 import LJC18A3
import time

sensor = LJC18A3({OUT})
while True:
    print('Object: %s' % ('YES' if sensor.detected() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
